title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Operator's Ledger (Bloomberg Terminal). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Operator's Ledger
options.thesis: The portfolio that proves P&L fluency by displaying it. Not a story about an operator; the interface of one.
options.viewport: Name in medium weight, positioning line below, four metric tiles spanning full width (one per case study, each showing headline number and one-line label), CTA below. No hero image. The numbers ARE the hero.
options.risk: Reads cold or sterile if type is too small or spacing too tight. Density must be purposeful, not overwhelming.

raised.raise: Grid discipline: every element snaps to a visible grid.
Flat commitment to solid color. No gradients, no glass.
Single vertical axis ruling all content below the fold.
One warm amber accent as the single focal element amid neutral density.
Limited palette: three colors maximum (ground, type, functional accent).

options.label: The Deal Memo
options.thesis: The format the audience reads fifty times a week. Thesis at the top, evidence below, structured for the cross-check scan.
options.viewport: Name and title, one-sentence thesis, then immediately into the first case study summary with headline metric. Clean serif headings, systematic sans body.
options.risk: The direction most runs in this category land on. Familiar and effective, but could be indistinguishable from a well-designed LinkedIn long-form post.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Four instruments, each showing one truth about the operator. The cross-check sweep is the reading order.
options.viewport: Four gauge-like regions, each owning one case study metric and capability label. Matte black ground, luminous white markings, one green confirmation accent.
options.case: Holds audience identification through the operator metaphor (cross-checking, calm under pressure). Loses product clarity because matte black aviation aesthetic fights readable long-form decision narratives on inner pages.
options.risk: Aviation aesthetic is niche. Works for the landing page but may not extend to text-heavy About and Case Study pages.

options.label: Neubrutalist Grid
options.case: Reads as designer/creative culture. A VP at a PE-backed B2B SaaS company would find this jarring.
options.kept: Grid discipline: every element snaps to a visible grid.

options.label: Starship Panel
options.case: Sci-fi aesthetic with zero overlap with executive business culture.
options.kept: Flat commitment to solid color blocks, no gradients.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.case: Beautiful but too metaphorical for executive due diligence. The metaphor sits between visitor and information.
options.kept: Single vertical axis ruling every line of content.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.case: Whimsical and artistic. Reads as creative/animation culture, not executive operator culture.
options.kept: One warm accent element as the single focal point.

options.label: Risograph Web System
options.case: Print/design culture with zero connection for a B2B hiring manager.
options.kept: Limited palette discipline: two or three colors maximum.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Minimal white background, clean sans-serif, hero with name and title, grid of project cards. What every portfolio template ships.
canonCard.viewport: Name, title, one-line bio, then a 2x2 grid of project cards with hover effects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design. Every portfolio builder ships this.
